# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment

The incumbent is already timing-feasible at WNS 0.579 ns and WHS 0.052 ns, with 8 LUTs and 8 FFs. The objective is strictly fewer LUTs, or equal LUTs with fewer FFs; there is no evidence of a prior optimization attempt. The current RTL registers an 8-bit, four-way mux output with synchronous active-high reset. Its top-level numeric latency is unknown, so preserve its observed cycle behavior without adding a numeric latency annotation. In chip-top implementation, pad delay is included in routed timing.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the `case` mux with a one-hot decode and per-bit masked-OR selection may reduce LUT usage by mapping the selection into compact 7-series LUT logic while retaining the same output register and reset behavior.

## Instruction for generator

In `mux4`, replace the `case (sel)` data selection with a combinational one-hot decode of all four `sel` values and an 8-bit bitwise-AND/OR masked selection of `a`, `b`, `c`, and `d`. Keep `y` assigned only on the rising edge of `clk`, with synchronous active-high reset taking priority and clearing all 8 bits. Preserve the exact ports and selection mapping; do not add registers, change latency, or add a numeric `@latency` annotation.
